claim: Burg Landshut above Bernkastel-Kues is a 13th-century summer residence of the Archbishops of Trier built on a late-Roman 'Princastellum' fort, with a 30 m keep, barrier-free circular path, on-site restaurant and panoramic Mosel views; reachable on foot in ~30 min from the market square, by car, or by the yellow Burg Landshut Express.
quote: unusually massive remains of a Roman fortification (fort)... dominates the hilltop above Bernkastel with its impressive 30-meter-high keep and fortress walls... barrier-free circular route around the grounds

claim: Burg Landshut was destroyed by fire in 1692, sits about a half-hour walk from Bernkastel-Kues old town, and entry to the castle grounds is free with only a small fee to climb the tower.
quote: built in the 13th century as a summer residence for the Archbishops of Trier, and it was destroyed by fire in 1692... Entry to the castle grounds is free, with only a small fee to climb the tower.

claim: The Oberburg Manderscheid, first recorded 1141-1146 and destroyed by French troops in 1673, is a freely accessible ruin with a five-storey bergfried visitors can climb for views over the Niederburg and the Lieser valley.
quote: Ruins with a five-story fighting tower (bergfried) that visitors can access... destroyed by French troops in 1673... thoroughly renovated in 1921 by the municipality of Manderscheid

claim: The Niederburg Manderscheid, owned since 1899 by the Eifelverein, opens April 1 – October 31 from 10:30-17:00 (closed Tuesdays) and hosts the popular annual Manderscheider Burgenfest medieval festival on the last August weekend.
quote: Summer hours (April 1–October 31): 10:30 a.m.–5 p.m.... A medieval festival occurs annually the last August weekend, attracting approximately 15,000 visitors and featuring a jousting field.

claim: Grevenburg above Traben-Trarbach was built in 1350 by Count Johann III of Sponheim-Starkenburg, changed hands 13 times during 17th-18th century wars, and was finally destroyed by the French in 1734 — today an ~700 m² ruin reached by a ~30-min climb from Trarbach with a castle tavern in season.
quote: The castle was built in 1350 by the Count Johann III of Sponheim-Starkenburg... the castle changed hands 13 times... destroyed by the French in 1734... extending over an area of around 700 square metres.

claim: Grevenburg ruins are freely accessible year-round and feature a seasonal castle tavern and garden with sweeping views over the Mosel loop.
quote: Today, visitors can explore the castle ruins, which feature a cozy tavern and castle garden integrated into the remaining structures. The location offers scenic vistas overlooking the Mosel River valley.

claim: Burg Arras near Alf was a Roman border station and imperial castle; today the Keuthen family runs it as a 10-room castle hotel, restaurant and museum, with day visits Saturday-Monday from 11:00 (reservation required), museum admission €6, featuring the original castle dungeon and tower visit.
quote: the only castle hotel on the Mosel... admission priced at €6.00... Saturday, Sunday, Monday from 11:00 AM (reservation required)

claim: Burg Arras was destroyed by French troops during the War of the Austrian Succession and rebuilt over a century ago as a noble residence; the on-site museum is dedicated to former German President Dr. Heinrich Lübke and showcases local cultural treasures, the original dungeon and a tower visit.
quote: destroyed by the French during the War of the Austrian Succession, and was rebuilt more than 100 years ago as a noble residence... castle museum is dedicated to former German President Dr. Heinrich Lübke

claim: Marienburg above Pünderich/Zell perches on a peninsula inside the 14 km Mosel loop with three superimposed architectural layers (12th-century manor, late-Gothic 15th-c. choir, 18th-c. raised choir) and today operates as a youth education centre — visitable only from the outside.
quote: the manor house dates back to the 12th century, the late Gothic choir from the second half of the 15th century, and the elevated choir masonry with oval windows from the 18th century... Marienburg is a youth education center and can only be visited from the outside.

claim: The Prinzenkopfturm, a ~10-minute walk from Marienburg, is freely accessible day and night and is considered one of the most beautiful viewpoints on the Mosel, looking down on the Pünderich hillside viaduct and the Zeller Hamm bend.
quote: the Prinzenkopf observation tower, approximately 10 minutes' walk from Marienburg Castle, is considered one of the most beautiful vantage points on the Moselle. The Prinzenkopf Tower is open at all times.

claim: Schloss Lieser, designed by Heinrich Theodor Schmidt in 1884-1887 for industrialist Eduard Puricelli and enlarged for his son-in-law Clemens von Schorlemer in 1904-1906, combines a Neo-Renaissance block with a later Art Nouveau wing inspired by Palladian villas; Kaiser Wilhelm II stayed here in 1906, 1911 and 1913, and today it houses a 49-room Marriott Autograph Collection hotel.
quote: designed by architect Heinrich Theodor Schmidt in 1884–1887 as the residence for the family of winery owner Eduard Puricelli... Kaiser Wilhelm II stayed in 1906, 1911 and 1913.

claim: Schloss Lieser sits directly on the Mosel riverbank in the village of Lieser (~15 km from Dreis) and is open as a luxury hotel with restaurant, spa, indoor pool and library accessible to non-resident diners.
quote: Nestled in the heart of the Moselle Valley, directly on the riverbank and surrounded by vineyards... 49 luxurious and individually appointed guest rooms and suites.

claim: Burg Eltz, the famously intact fairy-tale Mosel castle, sits ~62 km / 1 h 3 min by car from Wittlich and therefore falls outside the 30 km radius from Dreis — it is a feasible half-day outing but not a 'local' detour.
quote: The distance between Wittlich to Burg Eltz is 36 miles, with a road distance of 38.3 miles (approximately 62 km). The fastest way to get from Wittlich to Burg Eltz is to drive which takes 1 hour 3 minutes.
